trajectory_summary: This call moves from a normal, cooperative verify flow into a self-inflicted disqualification: the rep, looking at Google Maps, decides the property has too many trees and talks himself (and the customer) out of the appointment without any documented protocol for doing so. The customer never objected to booking — the rep manufactured the exit himself, and the call ends in under two minutes with no appointment and no path forward explored.
outcome_dispute: If v1 tagged this as a standard DQ, that undersells what happened: this is a rep self-disqualifying a lead based on his own read of a satellite map and a same-call verbal exchange, not a documented hard-gate answer (e.g., roof age, ownership, credit). The schema's dq_rules do not include 'rep's visual impression of tree density from Google Maps' as a qualifying hard gate — the closer/design team is who actually assesses shading via satellite/roof survey. This looks like a setter making a technical, closer-tier judgment call prematurely and killing a lead that a specialist should have evaluated.
